title: As an intended voucher recipient, I want to access a voucher after my claim is recorded, so that I can retrieve the digital fallback later.
body:
### User Story Title
As an intended voucher recipient, I want to access a voucher after my claim is recorded, so that I can retrieve the digital fallback later.

### Description
Covers retrieval of a voucher after the recipient completes the claim flow. This story belongs to [Functional Idea #97](https://github.com/Sebasriquelme10/Software-Requeriments/issues/97) and implements [UC02: Claim a Digital Fallback Voucher (#295)](https://github.com/Sebasriquelme10/Software-Requeriments/issues/295).

### Acceptance Criteria
- **Given / Successful Behavior:** Given the recipient has a successfully recorded claim, when they access the claimed voucher, then the system makes it available to them.
- **Alternate / Edge Cases:** If the claim is absent or not confirmed, access behavior remains unresolved.
- **Error / Failure Behavior:** If the claimed voucher cannot be retrieved, do not present it as successfully loaded; recovery behavior is unresolved.
- **Unresolved Business Decisions:** How claimed vouchers are presented; claim expiry; voucher terms; how this differs from UC01 access.

### Implementation Details
#### Frontend
- **UI Behavior & Interactions:** Provide a route from a confirmed claim to the recipient’s voucher view; content and navigation are undecided.
- **Components & Forms:** Depend on the approved interaction; none are prescribed.
- **States & Messages:** Distinguish available, unavailable, and failed states as applicable; exact messages remain undecided.
- **Navigation:** Follow the approved voucher flow; route details are unspecified.
#### Backend
- **APIs & Endpoint Specs:** No endpoint contract is established; define it after policy decisions.
- **Validations & Domain Rules:** Retrieve the voucher associated with the recipient’s confirmed claim and apply approved access rules.
- **Authorization & Security:** Apply only approved role and recipient-access rules.
- **Services & Integrations:** Use existing voucher/event capabilities if available; integrations need confirmation.
#### Database
- **Persistence & Entities:** Claim retention and access associations need confirmation; do not assume redemption fields.
- **Fields & Types:** Derive fields from approved business rules.
- **Relationships & Constraints:** Define event, voucher, recipient, and claim associations as applicable after privacy and eligibility decisions.
- **Data State Changes:** Distinguish attempted and completed issuance/claim/access operations.
### Test Notes
- **Happy Path Scenarios:** Retrieve a voucher for a recipient with a recorded claim.
- **Alternate & Edge Scenarios:** Check behavior when a claim is pending, missing, or no longer valid once rules are decided.
- **Failure & Error Recovery:** Simulate retrieval errors and ensure no success state is shown.
- **Test Types Needed:** Unit/domain, API/service, and UI integration tests as applicable.

title: As an intended voucher recipient, I want to claim a digital fallback voucher made available to me, so that I can secure the digital alternative when physical items run out.
body:
### User Story Title
As an intended voucher recipient, I want to claim a digital fallback voucher made available to me, so that I can secure the digital alternative when physical items run out.

### Description
Covers the recipient’s explicit claim action, distinct from issuance in UC01. This story belongs to [Functional Idea #97](https://github.com/Sebasriquelme10/Software-Requeriments/issues/97) and implements [UC02: Claim a Digital Fallback Voucher (#295)](https://github.com/Sebasriquelme10/Software-Requeriments/issues/295).

### Acceptance Criteria
- **Given / Successful Behavior:** Given a claimable voucher is available to an eligible recipient, when they choose to claim it, then the system records the claim and makes the voucher accessible.
- **Alternate / Edge Cases:** If vouchers are issued automatically rather than claimed, this flow may not apply; issuance mode is unresolved.
- **Error / Failure Behavior:** If the claim cannot be recorded, do not show it as completed; retry and duplicate-claim handling remain open.
- **Unresolved Business Decisions:** Whether claiming is required; eligibility; claim limits; voucher terms; whether claim reserves or redeems; expiration.

### Implementation Details
#### Frontend
- **UI Behavior & Interactions:** Show a claim action only under agreed eligibility and availability rules and present its outcome.
- **Components & Forms:** Depend on the approved interaction; none are prescribed.
- **States & Messages:** Distinguish available, unavailable, and failed states as applicable; exact messages remain undecided.
- **Navigation:** Follow the approved voucher flow; route details are unspecified.
#### Backend
- **APIs & Endpoint Specs:** No endpoint contract is established; define it after policy decisions.
- **Validations & Domain Rules:** Validate eligibility and availability and record the claim without treating it as redemption unless approved.
- **Authorization & Security:** Apply only approved role and recipient-access rules.
- **Services & Integrations:** Use existing voucher/event capabilities if available; integrations need confirmation.
#### Database
- **Persistence & Entities:** Claim persistence, uniqueness, voucher-recipient relation, and transaction rules are unresolved.
- **Fields & Types:** Derive fields from approved business rules.
- **Relationships & Constraints:** Define event, voucher, recipient, and claim associations as applicable after privacy and eligibility decisions.
- **Data State Changes:** Distinguish attempted and completed issuance/claim/access operations.
### Test Notes
- **Happy Path Scenarios:** Claim an available voucher and verify it becomes accessible to the recipient.
- **Alternate & Edge Scenarios:** Attempt a claim when no voucher is available or the actor is ineligible after rules are defined.
- **Failure & Error Recovery:** Force claim persistence failure and verify no false claim confirmation.
- **Test Types Needed:** Unit/domain, API/service, and UI integration tests as applicable.

title: As an intended voucher recipient, I want to access the digital fallback voucher provided to me, so that I can use the digital alternative.

- **Validations & Domain Rules:** Resolve the recipient-to-voucher association and apply approved access rules.
- **Authorization & Security:** Apply only approved role and recipient-access rules.
- **Services & Integrations:** Use existing voucher/event capabilities if available; integrations need confirmation.
#### Database

- **Relationships & Constraints:** Define event, voucher, recipient, and claim associations as applicable after privacy and eligibility decisions.

title: As a promotional-item manager, I want to issue a digital voucher when physical promotional items are confirmed depleted, so that recipients have a fallback.
body:
### User Story Title
As a promotional-item manager, I want to issue a digital voucher when physical promotional items are confirmed depleted, so that recipients have a fallback.

### Description
Initiates voucher issuance after depletion is confirmed. This story belongs to [Functional Idea #97](https://github.com/Sebasriquelme10/Software-Requeriments/issues/97) and implements [UC01: Issue Digital Fallback Vouchers (#124)](https://github.com/Sebasriquelme10/Software-Requeriments/issues/124).

### Acceptance Criteria
- **Given / Successful Behavior:** Given physical promotional items are confirmed depleted and the recipient is defined, when the responsible actor initiates issuance, then the system provides a digital fallback voucher for the intended recipient.
- **Alternate / Edge Cases:** If depletion or the intended recipient cannot be established, whether issuance is blocked or handled another way is unresolved.
- **Error / Failure Behavior:** If issuance fails, the voucher must not be represented as successfully issued; retry behavior is unresolved.
- **Unresolved Business Decisions:** Who manages issuance; how depletion is confirmed; recipient eligibility; voucher entitlements; issuance mode; redemption scope.

### Implementation Details
#### Frontend
- **UI Behavior & Interactions:** Provide an agreed issuance action and show the result; interface and states depend on approved rules.
- **Components & Forms:** Depend on the approved interaction; none are prescribed.
- **States & Messages:** Distinguish available, unavailable, and failed states as applicable; exact messages remain undecided.
- **Navigation:** Follow the approved voucher flow; route details are unspecified.
#### Backend
- **APIs & Endpoint Specs:** No endpoint contract is established; define it after policy decisions.
- **Validations & Domain Rules:** Validate depletion, recipient, and actor authorization after the business rules are approved; do not imply redemption.
- **Authorization & Security:** Apply only approved role and recipient-access rules.
- **Services & Integrations:** Use existing voucher/event capabilities if available; integrations need confirmation.
#### Database
- **Persistence & Entities:** Voucher issuance persistence and recipient association need schema and retention decisions.
- **Fields & Types:** Derive fields from approved business rules.
- **Relationships & Constraints:** Define event, voucher, recipient, and claim associations as applicable after privacy and eligibility decisions.
- **Data State Changes:** Distinguish attempted and completed issuance/claim/access operations.
### Test Notes
- **Happy Path Scenarios:** Issue a fallback voucher for a depleted promotion and make it available to its intended recipient.
- **Alternate & Edge Scenarios:** Check cases where depletion or recipient eligibility is uncertain once rules are established.
- **Failure & Error Recovery:** Simulate issuance failure and verify the voucher is not shown as successfully issued.
- **Test Types Needed:** Unit/domain, API/service, and UI integration tests as applicable.

title: UC02: Trace Serious Safety or Conduct Feedback
body:
**Name:** UC02: Trace Serious Safety or Conduct Feedback

**Description:** Allow an authorized administrator or reviewer to use administrative traceability information for feedback designated as involving a serious safety or conduct case. Submitting feedback anonymously is covered by UC01: Submit Anonymous Feedback (#128). The meaning and limits of anonymity, what can be traced, and the conditions for access remain unresolved.

**Primary Actor:** Authorized administrator or safety/conduct reviewer (role and authority are not specified).

**Supporting Actors:** Feedback submitter; administrative or safety/conduct process (not specified).

**Benefit:** The responsible actor can use available traceability information to follow up on a serious safety or conduct case while the feedback feature supports anonymous submission.

**Trigger:** An authorized actor identifies a feedback item as potentially involving a serious safety or conduct case and initiates a traceability review.

**Preconditions:**
- Feedback has been submitted under UC01 (#128).
- A case has been identified as meeting applicable serious-safety-or-conduct criteria; those criteria are not specified.
- The actor is authorized to access any applicable traceability information; access rules are not specified.

**Primary Flow:**
1. The actor selects feedback associated with a case designated for traceability review.
2. The actor initiates a review of the administrative traceability information available for that feedback.
3. The system presents only the traceability information permitted under applicable rules.

**Postconditions:** The authorized actor has reviewed available traceability information. Whether this identifies the submitter or results in further action is not specified.

**Alternate Flows:**
- Case does not meet criteria: If the case does not meet the eventual serious-case criteria, traceability access is not established by this Use Case; the outcome is not specified.

**Exception Flows:**
- Traceability information unavailable: The actor cannot complete the review; escalation or recovery behavior is not specified.

**Open Questions:**
- What constitutes a serious safety or conduct case, and who makes that determination?
- What does administrative traceability mean, and what information can be traced?
- Does traceability allow submitter identification, or does it only associate the feedback with a case or process?
- Who may authorize, access, and audit traceability reviews? What approvals are required?
- How is anonymity preserved in ordinary use, and what are its explicit limits or exceptions?
- What privacy, consent, retention, and audit requirements apply to traceability information?
- What follow-up action, if any, is in scope after traceability review?
- How does this Use Case relate to automatically screening abusive or threatening feedback (#104)?

**Source Functional Idea:** [Collect anonymous feedback with administrative traceability (#101)](https://github.com/Sebasriquelme10/Software-Requeriments/issues/101)
**Epic:** Feedback and Reviews
**Elicitation Source:** Brainstorming + Sponsor Interview

title: UC02: Claim a Digital Fallback Voucher
body:
**Name:** UC02: Claim a Digital Fallback Voucher

**Description:** Allow an intended recipient to claim a digital voucher made available as a fallback after physical promotional items are depleted. This Use Case covers the recipient's claim action; issuance of the fallback voucher is covered by UC01: Issue Digital Fallback Vouchers (#124). Voucher terms, eligibility, and redemption are not defined.

**Primary Actor:** Intended voucher recipient (student recipient is mentioned in UC01; eligibility is not confirmed).

**Supporting Actors:** Actor responsible for managing promotional items (role not specified); voucher-issuing process.

**Benefit:** The intended recipient can claim a digital alternative when physical promotional items are depleted.

**Trigger:** The intended recipient chooses to claim a digital voucher made available to them.

**Preconditions:**
- Physical promotional items have been determined to be depleted.
- A digital fallback voucher has been made available to the intended recipient.
- The recipient is eligible to claim it; eligibility rules are not specified.

**Primary Flow:**
1. The intended recipient accesses a digital fallback voucher made available to them.
2. The system presents the available voucher and the recipient's available claim action.
3. The recipient chooses to claim the voucher.
4. The system records the claim and makes the claimed voucher accessible to the recipient.

**Postconditions:** The recipient has claimed and can access the digital fallback voucher. Whether claiming reserves, issues, or redeems anything is not specified.

**Alternate Flows:**
- No voucher available: If no claimable voucher is available to the recipient, the claim cannot proceed; the system's response is not specified.

**Exception Flows:**
- Claim cannot be recorded: If the claim fails, the recipient does not complete the claim. Recovery behavior is not specified.

**Open Questions:**
- Is a recipient expected to claim a voucher, or is it issued automatically? How does this Use Case relate to UC01's issuance/access flow?
- Who qualifies as an intended recipient, and how is eligibility determined?
- What does the voucher entitle the recipient to, and is it a substitute for the physical item?
- How is the voucher offer delivered or made accessible?
- Can a recipient claim more than one voucher for an event or promotion?
- Does claiming reserve or redeem the voucher, or is redemption a separate Use Case?
- Are there expiration dates, claim windows, or quantity limits?

**Source Functional Idea:** [Provide digital fallback vouchers when physical items run out (#97)](https://github.com/Sebasriquelme10/Software-Requeriments/issues/97)
**Epic:** Community and Social Engagement
**Elicitation Source:** Sponsor Interview

title: As a student, I want to compare selected events side by side by their key attributes, so that I can review their details when deciding which events to attend.
body:
Description
This story covers comparing selected events by schedule, location, capacity, cost, and participation requirements, with unavailable attributes indicated as such.

Acceptance Criteria
Given / Successful Behavior
Given the student has selected enough events to compare, when the student chooses to compare them, the system presents the selected events side by side with their schedule, location, capacity, cost, and participation requirements.
The student can review the selected events and the presented attributes.
Alternate / Edge Cases
If an attribute is unavailable for an event, the system indicates that the attribute is unavailable.
Error / Failure Behavior
If the student has not selected enough events to compare, the system does not display a comparison.
Unresolved Business Decisions
How many events can be compared at one time?
Are all listed attributes always shown, or can the student choose which ones to compare?
What should be displayed when event information is incomplete?
Does comparison include a recommendation or ranking, or only present the selected information?
What is the minimum number of selected events required to compare?
Implementation Details
Frontend
UI Behavior & Interactions: Allow the student to select events and request a comparison. Present the selected events and listed attributes side by side. Exact selection and comparison interactions are unspecified.
Components & Forms: A selection mechanism and a side-by-side comparison view are in scope. Specific components, layout, and any forms are unspecified.
States & Messages: Indicate when an attribute is unavailable. Do not display a comparison when too few events are selected. Exact message text and behavior for incomplete event information are unresolved.
Navigation: The source does not specify how the student enters the comparison flow or returns from it.
Backend
APIs & Endpoint Specs: No API, endpoint, payload, or response structure is specified.
Validations & Domain Rules: The system must not display a comparison when the selected event count is insufficient. The required threshold and rules for incomplete information are unresolved.
Authorization & Security: The primary actor is a student. Further permissions or security rules are unspecified.
Services & Integrations: The Use Cases reference an event discovery system. Specific services or integrations are not specified.
Database
Persistence & Entities: The source refers to events and their comparison information. Specific entities or persistence changes are unspecified.
Fields & Types: The compared attributes are schedule, location, capacity, cost, and participation requirements; their storage fields and types are unspecified.
Relationships & Constraints: No relationships or constraints are specified.
Data State Changes: The flow describes selecting and viewing events; no persistent mutations or state changes are specified.
Test Notes
Happy Path Scenarios: Verify that a comparison of enough selected events presents the five listed attributes side by side.
Alternate & Edge Scenarios: Verify that an unavailable attribute is indicated for the relevant event.
Failure & Error Recovery: Verify that an insufficient selection does not display a comparison. Test behavior for incomplete event information only after that business decision is defined.
Test Types Needed: UI or end-to-end coverage for event selection and side-by-side presentation; unit or service tests for insufficient selections and unavailable attributes. API tests depend on an API design not specified here.

title: UC01: Submit Anonymous Feedback
body:
**Name:** Submit Anonymous Feedback

**Description:** Allow an attendee to submit feedback anonymously. The feedback’s subject, format, and any limits on anonymity are not specified.

**Primary Actor:** Attendee.

**Supporting Actors:** Not specified.

**Benefit:** The attendee can provide feedback without their identity being disclosed through the feedback submission. The exact meaning and limits of anonymity remain open.

**Trigger:** The attendee chooses to submit feedback.

**Preconditions:**
- A means of submitting feedback is available to the attendee.
- The attendee is eligible to submit feedback; eligibility is not specified.

**Primary Flow:**
1. The attendee accesses the feedback submission opportunity.
2. The attendee provides feedback.
3. The attendee submits the feedback anonymously.

**Postconditions:** Feedback has been submitted. How it is stored, who can access it, and whether the submitter can be identified under any circumstances are not specified.

**Alternate Flows:**
- None specified.

**Exception Flows:**
- None specified.

**Open Questions:**
- What does “anonymous” mean: is identity never collected, hidden from ordinary viewers, or potentially disclosed under defined conditions?
- What does “administrative traceability” mean? This remains an open question and is not treated as a separate Use Case at this stage.
- What must administrators be able to trace, and under what conditions?
- Who may access traceability information, and what qualifies as a serious safety or conduct case?
- What feedback formats and subjects are in scope?
- Does this apply to post-event feedback, mid-event ratings, comments, or all feedback types?
- Who is eligible to submit feedback?

**Source Functional Idea:** [Collect anonymous feedback with administrative traceability (#101)](https://github.com/Sebasriquelme10/Software-Requeriments/issues/101)

**Epic:** Feedback and Reviews

**Elicitation Source:** Brainstorming + Sponsor Interview

title: As an attendee, I want to submit feedback anonymously, so that I can share feedback without my identity being disclosed through ordinary feedback access.
body:
### User Story Title
As an attendee, I want to submit feedback anonymously, so that I can share feedback without my identity being disclosed through ordinary feedback access.

### Description
Covers anonymous feedback submission while the scope and limits of anonymity remain unresolved. This story belongs to [Functional Idea #101](https://github.com/Sebasriquelme10/Software-Requeriments/issues/101) and implements [UC01: Submit Anonymous Feedback (#128)](https://github.com/Sebasriquelme10/Software-Requeriments/issues/128).

### Acceptance Criteria
- **Given / Successful Behavior:** Given an attendee is eligible, when they submit feedback through the anonymous flow, then it is recorded without disclosing their identity through ordinary feedback access, subject to approved rules.
- **Alternate / Edge Cases:** Any permitted traceability exception must follow criteria and access rules not yet decided; no identity disclosure is assumed.
- **Error / Failure Behavior:** If submission fails, do not falsely confirm it and do not expose identifying information through failure handling.
- **Unresolved Business Decisions:** Meaning and limits of anonymity; identity data collected; serious-case exception; access, authorization, consent, retention, feedback type and eligibility.

### Implementation Details
#### Frontend
- **UI Behavior & Interactions:** Distinguish anonymous feedback from identified flows; exact disclosure and interaction requirements require approval.
- **Components & Forms:** Depend on the approved feedback/traceability workflow; none are prescribed.
- **States & Messages:** Distinguish submitted, permitted, unavailable, and denied states as applicable; exact messages remain undecided.
- **Navigation:** Follow the approved feedback and restricted review flow.
#### Backend
- **APIs & Endpoint Specs:** No endpoint contract is established; define it after policy decisions.
- **Validations & Domain Rules:** Implement the approved anonymity boundary and avoid exposing identity in ordinary retrieval; do not invent an exception mechanism.
- **Authorization & Security:** Apply approved anonymity, role, case-qualification, and privacy rules; do not infer exceptions.
- **Services & Integrations:** Use approved feedback and administrative review capabilities; external processes require confirmation.
#### Database
- **Persistence & Entities:** Identity separation, traceability data, access controls, and retention require privacy decisions before schema design.
- **Fields & Types:** Derive fields from approved privacy and governance rules.
- **Relationships & Constraints:** Define feedback, actor, traceability, and case associations only as approved.
- **Data State Changes:** Distinguish submitted feedback from a reviewed traceability case; preserve approved privacy boundaries.
### Test Notes
- **Happy Path Scenarios:** Submit feedback and verify ordinary feedback views do not disclose the submitter identity under the approved model.
- **Alternate & Edge Scenarios:** Test anonymity when traceability rules or eligibility conditions apply.
- **Failure & Error Recovery:** Test submission errors and ensure identity data is not leaked through errors or logs.
- **Test Types Needed:** Privacy-focused unit/API, authorization, and UI integration tests as applicable.

title: As an attendee, I want to understand the anonymity conditions before submitting feedback, so that I can decide whether to share it.
body:
### User Story Title
As an attendee, I want to understand the anonymity conditions before submitting feedback, so that I can decide whether to share it.

### Description
Covers presenting the approved anonymity boundary before submission. This story belongs to [Functional Idea #101](https://github.com/Sebasriquelme10/Software-Requeriments/issues/101) and implements [UC01: Submit Anonymous Feedback (#128)](https://github.com/Sebasriquelme10/Software-Requeriments/issues/128).

### Acceptance Criteria
- **Given / Successful Behavior:** Given the feedback flow is presented, when the attendee reviews anonymity information, then approved identity handling and serious-case exceptions are stated before submission.
- **Alternate / Edge Cases:** If anonymity conditions are undefined, the system cannot truthfully promise absolute anonymity; required behavior must be decided.
- **Error / Failure Behavior:** If privacy information cannot be displayed, whether submission is blocked or another action is offered remains unresolved.
- **Unresolved Business Decisions:** What anonymous means; traceability exceptions; collected information; consent/disclosure wording; who authorizes access.

### Implementation Details
#### Frontend
- **UI Behavior & Interactions:** Present approved anonymity information before submission; wording and acknowledgment requirements are unresolved.
- **Components & Forms:** Depend on the approved feedback/traceability workflow; none are prescribed.
- **States & Messages:** Distinguish submitted, permitted, unavailable, and denied states as applicable; exact messages remain undecided.
- **Navigation:** Follow the approved feedback and restricted review flow.
#### Backend
- **APIs & Endpoint Specs:** No endpoint contract is established; define it after policy decisions.
- **Validations & Domain Rules:** Serve accurate privacy and traceability terms and do not overstate anonymity.
- **Authorization & Security:** Apply approved anonymity, role, case-qualification, and privacy rules; do not infer exceptions.
- **Services & Integrations:** Use approved feedback and administrative review capabilities; external processes require confirmation.
#### Database
- **Persistence & Entities:** Versioning or recording acceptance of terms is not assumed and requires a decision.
- **Fields & Types:** Derive fields from approved privacy and governance rules.
- **Relationships & Constraints:** Define feedback, actor, traceability, and case associations only as approved.
- **Data State Changes:** Distinguish submitted feedback from a reviewed traceability case; preserve approved privacy boundaries.
### Test Notes
- **Happy Path Scenarios:** Verify the attendee can review approved anonymity conditions before submission.
- **Alternate & Edge Scenarios:** Check changed terms, absent policy, and whether acknowledgment is required after decisions.
- **Failure & Error Recovery:** Test unavailable privacy information and verify the flow does not claim conditions were shown.
- **Test Types Needed:** Privacy-focused unit/API, authorization, and UI integration tests as applicable.

title: As an authorized administrator, I want to review available traceability information for feedback designated as a serious safety or conduct case, so that the case can be followed up appropriately.
body:
### User Story Title
As an authorized administrator, I want to review available traceability information for feedback designated as a serious safety or conduct case, so that the case can be followed up appropriately.

### Description
Covers authorized review of traceability information for a designated serious case. This story belongs to [Functional Idea #101](https://github.com/Sebasriquelme10/Software-Requeriments/issues/101) and implements [UC02: Trace Serious Safety or Conduct Feedback (#299)](https://github.com/Sebasriquelme10/Software-Requeriments/issues/299).

### Acceptance Criteria
- **Given / Successful Behavior:** Given an authorized actor and feedback designated under approved serious-case criteria, when the actor initiates a traceability review, then the system presents the traceability information permitted for that case.
- **Alternate / Edge Cases:** If the case does not meet approved criteria, traceability review is not available; who determines eligibility remains unresolved.
- **Error / Failure Behavior:** If traceability information is unavailable, do not imply the case was traced; escalation and recovery behavior are unresolved.
- **Unresolved Business Decisions:** Serious-case definition; who designates a case; what information is traced; whether identity is revealed; authorization and audit; privacy, consent, retention.

### Implementation Details
#### Frontend
- **UI Behavior & Interactions:** Provide a restricted review entry point only after actor/case rules are approved; do not expose identity by default.
- **Components & Forms:** Depend on the approved feedback/traceability workflow; none are prescribed.
- **States & Messages:** Distinguish submitted, permitted, unavailable, and denied states as applicable; exact messages remain undecided.
- **Navigation:** Follow the approved feedback and restricted review flow.
#### Backend
- **APIs & Endpoint Specs:** No endpoint contract is established; define it after policy decisions.
- **Validations & Domain Rules:** Enforce approved case qualification and authorization before returning traceability data.
- **Authorization & Security:** Apply approved anonymity, role, case-qualification, and privacy rules; do not infer exceptions.
- **Services & Integrations:** Use approved feedback and administrative review capabilities; external processes require confirmation.
#### Database
- **Persistence & Entities:** Traceability records, access history, retention, and relation to feedback require governance decisions.
- **Fields & Types:** Derive fields from approved privacy and governance rules.
- **Relationships & Constraints:** Define feedback, actor, traceability, and case associations only as approved.
- **Data State Changes:** Distinguish submitted feedback from a reviewed traceability case; preserve approved privacy boundaries.
### Test Notes
- **Happy Path Scenarios:** Review permitted traceability information for a qualifying case as an authorized actor.
- **Alternate & Edge Scenarios:** Test a nonqualifying case and an actor without required authority.
- **Failure & Error Recovery:** Simulate unavailable traceability data and ensure no completed-review state is shown.
- **Test Types Needed:** Privacy-focused unit/API, authorization, and UI integration tests as applicable.

### User Story Title

### Acceptance Criteria
- **Given / Successful Behavior:** Given a traceability request, when the system evaluates the case and actor under approved rules, then it provides only information permitted for a qualifying case.
- **Alternate / Edge Cases:** If qualification or authority cannot be confirmed, whether access is denied or escalated follows a rule not yet defined.
- **Error / Failure Behavior:** On authorization or qualification lookup failure, do not grant traceability access by default.
- **Unresolved Business Decisions:** Qualifying-case thresholds; reviewer roles; approvals; scope of trace information; whether submitter identity is ever revealed; auditing and escalation.

### Implementation Details
#### Frontend
- **UI Behavior & Interactions:** Communicate access unavailable without revealing protected traceability details; denial states need definition.
- **Components & Forms:** Depend on the approved feedback/traceability workflow; none are prescribed.
- **States & Messages:** Distinguish submitted, permitted, unavailable, and denied states as applicable; exact messages remain undecided.

#### Backend
- **APIs & Endpoint Specs:** No endpoint contract is established; define it after policy decisions.
- **Validations & Domain Rules:** Apply fail-closed authorization and qualification checks according to approved policy; do not infer a de-anonymization mechanism.
- **Authorization & Security:** Apply approved anonymity, role, case-qualification, and privacy rules; do not infer exceptions.
- **Services & Integrations:** Use approved feedback and administrative review capabilities; external processes require confirmation.
#### Database
- **Persistence & Entities:** Access-control and audit storage requirements must be defined; no audit schema is assumed.
- **Fields & Types:** Derive fields from approved privacy and governance rules.
- **Relationships & Constraints:** Define feedback, actor, traceability, and case associations only as approved.
- **Data State Changes:** Distinguish submitted feedback from a reviewed traceability case; preserve approved privacy boundaries.
### Test Notes
- **Happy Path Scenarios:** Confirm a qualified reviewer receives only approved traceability information.
- **Alternate & Edge Scenarios:** Check unqualified cases, unauthorized roles, and incomplete authority data.
- **Failure & Error Recovery:** Simulate qualification or authorization failure and verify access is not granted.
- **Test Types Needed:** Privacy-focused unit/API, authorization, and UI integration tests as applicable.
